meta_description: A free guide to moving from cybersecurity into AI security, by Zulia Shavaeva. Find a learning path, plan your study and practise with exercises.

hero.sub:
Hi, I'm Zulia. I look after security for the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center in EMEA.

I started as a developer, then moved into security, risk and compliance. Learning AI security took a lot of study, and people often ask me where to start.

So I made a free guide to help security people make that move. It's my way of giving back. I hope you find it useful.

help_intro: The guide is free to use, with no account needed. Take the quiz for a suggested starting point, or browse the paths yourself.

help.title: Find a starting point
help.body: Answer 16 questions about your experience and interests. The quiz suggests a path and a study plan. It is a guide, not a skills assessment.

help.title: Choose a learning path
help.body: Seven paths cover engineering, red teaming, architecture, governance, compliance, consulting and research. Each includes resources and an exercise you can use for practice.

help.title: Build the skills you need
help.body: Browse 13 skill pages with reading, exercises and practice questions. Free resources come first. Optional paid courses are listed separately.

about: I'm the Security Leader for the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center in EMEA. I review AI systems for security risks and work with delivery teams to address them.

My route here started in software development. I taught algorithms and data structures at Durham University, where I studied Computer Science, before joining AWS in DevOps. I later moved into security, risk and compliance, and now focus on AI security.

Much of my work is about protecting data and controlling what AI systems can access. That includes data residency and retention, agent permissions, and the evidence teams need for security and compliance reviews.
I also help run AWS Cloud Women Manchester and mentor women moving into cloud and security. Teaching has been part of my work since university. This guide is another way to share what I've learned.
